title: Chapter 5: Embeddings, Vector Databases, and Semantic Search
content:
Chapter 5: Embeddings, Vector Databases, and Semantic Search

Opening Hook: Search by Meaning, Not Just Words

In Chapter 4, you built your first RAG assistant.

It could load a PDF, split it into chunks, retrieve relevant chunks, and answer questions using document context.

That was a major step.

But the retrieval method was simple.

It mostly looked for overlapping words.

That works when the user’s question uses the same words as the document.

For example:

Question: What is the refund policy? Document chunk: The refund policy allows customers to request a refund within 30 days.

Keyword retrieval works well here because the word “refund” appears in both places.

But what if the user asks:

Can customers get their money back?

The document may still say:

The refund policy allows customers to request a refund within 30 days.

A keyword search may miss the connection because the words are different.

The meaning is similar, but the wording is not.

This is where embeddings and semantic search become useful.

Semantic search means search by meaning.

Instead of asking:

Do these words match?

semantic search asks:

Do these ideas mean something similar?

In this chapter, you will build a personal knowledge search engine.

It will take notes, split them into chunks, create embeddings, store them in a vector database, and search them by meaning.

This is the next major step toward stronger RAG systems.

What You Will Learn

By the end of this chapter, you will understand:

  • What embeddings are
  • Why embeddings are useful
  • What semantic search means
  • What vector databases do
  • How similarity search works
  • How to store text chunks with metadata
  • How to build a personal knowledge search engine
  • How embeddings improve RAG retrieval
  • How to test text processing logic without live API calls
  • How this project can become a portfolio or freelance asset

Why This Chapter Matters

A RAG system is only as good as its retrieval.

If retrieval finds the wrong chunks, the model may answer poorly.

If retrieval finds the right chunks, the model has a much better chance of giving a useful answer.

Chapter 4 used keyword retrieval because it made the RAG pattern easy to understand.

This chapter upgrades retrieval.

You will learn the pattern used by many modern document assistants:

Documents ↓ Chunks ↓ Embeddings ↓ Vector database ↓ Semantic search ↓ Relevant context ↓ LLM answer

This pattern is used in:

  • Internal knowledge bots
  • PDF chat assistants
  • Customer support assistants
  • Research tools
  • Developer documentation search
  • Study assistants
  • Business document Q&A systems

Embeddings and vector databases are core AI engineering skills.

5.1 What Is an Embedding?

An embedding is a numeric representation of text.

For example, the sentence:

Customers can request a refund within 30 days.

can be converted into a list of numbers.

That list might look conceptually like this:

[0.12, -0.04, 0.88, 0.31, ...]

The actual list is usually much longer.

You do not need to understand every number.

The important idea is this:

Text with similar meaning gets similar numeric representations.

For example:

Customers can request a refund.

and:

Customers can get their money back.

may produce embeddings that are close to each other.

That is what makes semantic search possible.

5.2 What Is Semantic Search?

Semantic search finds results based on meaning.

Keyword search looks for matching words.

Semantic search looks for similar ideas.

Example:

Query: How can users reset their password? Document: Account recovery is available from the login page.

Keyword search may struggle because “reset password” and “account recovery” are different words.

Semantic search may understand that these ideas are related.

This makes it better for natural language questions.

5.3 What Is a Vector Database?

A vector database stores embeddings and lets you search by similarity.

A normal database might store:

name email date price status

A vector database stores:

text chunk embedding vector metadata

When you ask a question, the app creates an embedding for the question.

Then it searches for text chunks whose embeddings are most similar.

The flow looks like this:

User question ↓ Question embedding ↓ Vector database search ↓ Most similar chunks ↓ LLM answer

In this chapter, you will use Chroma as a beginner-friendly local vector database.

5.4 Similarity Search

Similarity search compares vectors.

The goal is to find which stored vectors are closest to the query vector.

You do not need to implement advanced vector math yourself in this chapter.

The vector database handles it.

At a high level:

Query: "How do I get a refund?" ↓ Embedding: [numbers] ↓ Compare against stored chunk embeddings ↓ Return closest chunks

This is what powers semantic retrieval.

5.5 Embeddings vs LLMs

Embeddings and LLMs are different.

FeatureEmbedding ModelLLM
Main jobConvert text into vectorsGenerate text
OutputNumbersWords
Used forSearch, clustering, similarityAnswers, summaries, reasoning
ExampleFind relevant document chunksExplain retrieved chunks

In a RAG app, you often use both.

Embedding model → finds relevant chunks LLM → writes the answer

5.6 Why This Improves RAG

In Chapter 4, retrieval depended on keyword overlap.

In this chapter, retrieval uses meaning.

That means the app can find related chunks even when the user uses different words.

Example:

User: Can I get my money back? Document: Refunds are available within 30 days.

Semantic search is more likely to connect these ideas.

This makes the document assistant feel smarter and more natural.

5.7 Project: Personal Knowledge Search Engine

What This Project Does

This project builds a local semantic search engine for your notes.

It will:

  1. Load .txt and .md files from a notes folder
  2. Split them into chunks
  3. Create embeddings for each chunk
  4. Store chunks in a local Chroma database
  5. Search notes by meaning
  6. Display matching chunks with source information

Who This Helps

This project helps:

  • Students searching study notes
  • Developers searching technical notes
  • Freelancers searching project notes
  • Writers searching research notes
  • Professionals searching personal knowledge bases
  • AI builders improving RAG retrieval

What You Will Build

Create this project structure:

chapter_05_semantic_search/ notes/ example_note.md chroma_db/ .env.example .gitignore requirements.txt llm_client.py note_loader.py text_utils.py embedding_client.py vector_store.py search_app.py test_note_loader.py test_text_utils.py test_vector_store_helpers.py README.md

5.8 Setup

Step 1: Create the Folder

mkdir chapter_05_semantic_search cd chapter_05_semantic_search mkdir notes chroma_db

Step 2: Create a Virtual Environment

python -m venv .venv

Activate it.

On macOS or Linux:

source .venv/bin/activate

On Windows PowerShell:

.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

Step 3: Create requirements.txt

openai python-dotenv chromadb pytest

Install dependencies:

pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 4: Create .env.example

OPENAI_API_KEY=replace_with_your_api_key OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small CHROMA_PATH=chroma_db COLLECTION_NAME=personal_notes

Copy it to .env.

On macOS or Linux:

cp .env.example .env

On Windows PowerShell:

Copy-Item .env.example .env

Then edit .env and add your real API key.

Never publish your real .env file.

Model names, pricing, and provider behavior may change. Before publishing or deploying, verify current provider documentation.

5.9 File: .gitignore

Create .gitignore:

.env .venv/ __pycache__/ .pytest_cache/ *.pyc *.log chroma_db/

The local vector database is generated data, so it does not need to be committed.

5.10 File: notes/example_note.md

Create a sample note:

# Agentic AI With Python Notes AI agents are software systems that use language models, tools, memory, and workflows to help complete user goals. RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It retrieves relevant information before generating an answer. Tool calling allows an AI assistant to use approved functions, such as calculators, search tools, or APIs. Memory helps an assistant remember useful context, but it must be designed carefully to protect privacy. Guardrails are checks and rules that help reduce risky behavior, unsupported claims, and unsafe actions.

This gives you something to search.

5.11 File: llm_client.py

This project mostly needs embeddings, but you may later use the same LLM client for answer generation.

Create llm_client.py:

""" Reusable LLM client for Chapter 5. This file is included for consistency with later RAG projects. """ import os from dataclasses import dataclass, field from dotenv import load_dotenv from openai import OpenAI load_dotenv() def get_env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float: """Read a float from an environment variable safely.""" raw_value = os.getenv(name) if raw_value is None: return default try: return float(raw_value) except ValueError: return default @dataclass class LLMConfig: """Configuration for the LLM client.""" model: str = field( default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4.1-mini") ) temperature: float = field( default_factory=lambda: get_env_float("OPENAI_TEMPERATURE", 0.2) ) class LLMClient: """Reusable client for text generation.""" def __init__(self, config: LLMConfig | None = None): self.config = config or LLMConfig() api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") if not api_key: raise ValueError( "OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add it to your .env file." ) self.client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key) def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: """Send a request to the model and return text output.""" if not system.strip(): raise ValueError("System instruction cannot be empty.") if not user.strip(): raise ValueError("User request cannot be empty.") model_input = f""" System instruction: {system.strip()} User request: {user.strip()} """ response = self.client.responses.create( model=self.config.model, input=model_input, temperature=self.config.temperature, ) return response.output_text Not executed automatically: requires live API credentials, network access, or external service.

5.12 File: note_loader.py

This file loads text and Markdown notes.

Create note_loader.py:

""" Note loading utilities for the Chapter 5 semantic search project. """ from dataclasses import dataclass from pathlib import Path SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {".txt", ".md"} @dataclass class NoteDocument: """A loaded note document.""" path: str text: str def is_supported_file(path: Path) -> bool: """Return True if a file extension is supported.""" return path.suffix.lower() in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS def load_note_file(path: Path) -> NoteDocument: """Load a single note file.""" if not path.exists(): raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {path}") if not path.is_file(): raise ValueError(f"Path is not a file: {path}") if not is_supported_file(path): raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file type: {path.suffix}") text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") return NoteDocument( path=str(path), text=text, ) def load_notes_from_folder(folder: str) -> list[NoteDocument]: """Load all supported notes from a folder.""" folder_path = Path(folder) if not folder_path.exists(): raise FileNotFoundError(f"Folder not found: {folder}") if not folder_path.is_dir(): raise ValueError(f"Path is not a folder: {folder}") documents = [] for path in sorted(folder_path.rglob("*")): if path.is_file() and is_supported_file(path): documents.append(load_note_file(path)) return documents Test result: Python syntax check passed.

5.13 File: text_utils.py

This file chunks notes and creates chunk records.

Create text_utils.py:

""" Text utilities for Chapter 5 semantic search. """ from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass class TextChunk: """A chunk of text with source metadata.""" id: str text: str source: str chunk_index: int def clean_text(text: str) -> str: """Normalize whitespace.""" return " ".join(text.split()) def chunk_text( text: str, chunk_size: int = 800, overlap: int = 120, ) -> list[str]: """Split text into overlapping chunks.""" if chunk_size <= 0: raise ValueError("chunk_size must be greater than 0.") if overlap < 0: raise ValueError("overlap cannot be negative.") if overlap >= chunk_size: raise ValueError("overlap must be smaller than chunk_size.") cleaned = clean_text(text) if not cleaned: return [] chunks = [] start = 0 while start < len(cleaned): end = start + chunk_size chunk = cleaned[start:end].strip() if chunk: chunks.append(chunk) start = end - overlap return chunks def create_chunks_for_document( source: str, text: str, chunk_size: int = 800, overlap: int = 120, ) -> list[TextChunk]: """Create TextChunk objects for one document.""" raw_chunks = chunk_text( text=text, chunk_size=chunk_size, overlap=overlap, ) chunks = [] for index, chunk in enumerate(raw_chunks): chunk_id = f"{source}::chunk_{index}" chunks.append( TextChunk( id=chunk_id, text=chunk, source=source, chunk_index=index, ) ) return chunks Test result: Python syntax check passed.

5.14 File: embedding_client.py

This file creates embeddings using an API.

Create embedding_client.py:

""" Embedding client for Chapter 5 semantic search. """ import os from dataclasses import dataclass, field from dotenv import load_dotenv from openai import OpenAI load_dotenv() @dataclass class EmbeddingConfig: """Configuration for embedding generation.""" model: str = field( default_factory=lambda: os.getenv( "OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "text-embedding-3-small", ) ) class EmbeddingClient: """Client for creating text embeddings.""" def __init__(self, config: EmbeddingConfig | None = None): self.config = config or EmbeddingConfig() api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") if not api_key: raise ValueError( "OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add it to your .env file." ) self.client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key) def embed_text(self, text: str) -> list[float]: """Create an embedding for one text string.""" if not text.strip(): raise ValueError("Text cannot be empty.") response = self.client.embeddings.create( model=self.config.model, input=text, ) return response.data[0].embedding def embed_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]: """Create embeddings for multiple text strings.""" cleaned = [text for text in texts if text.strip()] if not cleaned: raise ValueError("At least one non-empty text is required.") response = self.client.embeddings.create( model=self.config.model, input=cleaned, ) return [item.embedding for item in response.data] Not executed automatically: requires live API credentials, network access, or external service.

5.15 File: vector_store.py

This file stores and searches chunks with Chroma.

Create vector_store.py:

""" Vector store utilities using Chroma for Chapter 5. """ import os from dataclasses import asdict from dotenv import load_dotenv import chromadb from embedding_client import EmbeddingClient from text_utils import TextChunk load_dotenv() def get_chroma_path() -> str: """Return local Chroma database path.""" return os.getenv("CHROMA_PATH", "chroma_db") def get_collection_name() -> str: """Return Chroma collection name.""" return os.getenv("COLLECTION_NAME", "personal_notes") def create_chroma_client(): """Create a persistent Chroma client.""" return chromadb.PersistentClient(path=get_chroma_path()) def get_or_create_collection(): """Get or create the Chroma collection.""" client = create_chroma_client() return client.get_or_create_collection(name=get_collection_name()) def chunk_to_metadata(chunk: TextChunk) -> dict: """Convert a TextChunk into metadata.""" data = asdict(chunk) return { "source": data["source"], "chunk_index": data["chunk_index"], } def add_chunks_to_vector_store( chunks: list[TextChunk], embedding_client: EmbeddingClient | None = None, ) -> int: """ Add text chunks to the vector store. Returns the number of chunks added. """ if not chunks: return 0 embedder = embedding_client or EmbeddingClient() collection = get_or_create_collection() texts = [chunk.text for chunk in chunks] embeddings = embedder.embed_texts(texts) collection.add( ids=[chunk.id for chunk in chunks], documents=texts, embeddings=embeddings, metadatas=[chunk_to_metadata(chunk) for chunk in chunks], ) return len(chunks) def search_vector_store( query: str, top_k: int = 5, embedding_client: EmbeddingClient | None = None, ) -> list[dict]: """ Search the vector store by semantic similarity. """ if not query.strip(): raise ValueError("Query cannot be empty.") if top_k <= 0: raise ValueError("top_k must be greater than 0.") embedder = embedding_client or EmbeddingClient() collection = get_or_create_collection() query_embedding = embedder.embed_text(query) results = collection.query( query_embeddings=[query_embedding], n_results=top_k, ) output = [] ids = results.get("ids", [[]])[0] documents = results.get("documents", [[]])[0] metadatas = results.get("metadatas", [[]])[0] distances = results.get("distances", [[]])[0] for index, doc_id in enumerate(ids): output.append( { "id": doc_id, "text": documents[index], "metadata": metadatas[index], "distance": distances[index] if index < len(distances) else None, } ) return output def format_search_results(results: list[dict]) -> str: """Format search results for display.""" if not results: return "No results found." lines = [] for index, result in enumerate(results, start=1): metadata = result.get("metadata") or {} source = metadata.get("source", "unknown source") chunk_index = metadata.get("chunk_index", "unknown") lines.append(f"Result {index}") lines.append(f"Source: {source}") lines.append(f"Chunk: {chunk_index}") lines.append(f"Distance: {result.get('distance')}") lines.append("") lines.append(result.get("text", "")) lines.append("-" * 60) return "\n".join(lines) Test result: Python syntax check passed.

5.16 File: search_app.py

This is the command-line app.

Create search_app.py:

""" Chapter 5 Project: Personal Knowledge Search Engine This app indexes notes and searches them by meaning. """ from note_loader import load_notes_from_folder from text_utils import create_chunks_for_document from vector_store import ( add_chunks_to_vector_store, search_vector_store, format_search_results, ) def index_notes(notes_folder: str = "notes") -> None: """Load, chunk, embed, and store notes.""" print(f"\nLoading notes from: {notes_folder}") documents = load_notes_from_folder(notes_folder) if not documents: print("No supported notes found.") return all_chunks = [] for document in documents: chunks = create_chunks_for_document( source=document.path, text=document.text, ) all_chunks.extend(chunks) print(f"Created {len(all_chunks)} chunk(s).") print("Creating embeddings and adding to vector store...") added = add_chunks_to_vector_store(all_chunks) print(f"Added {added} chunk(s) to vector store.") def search_loop() -> None: """Run interactive semantic search.""" print("\nSemantic Search") print("=" * 40) print("Type a question or search query.") print("Type /exit to quit.") print("=" * 40) while True: query = input("\nSearch: ").strip() if query.lower() in {"/exit", "exit", "quit"}: print("Goodbye.") break if not query: print("Please enter a search query.") continue try: results = search_vector_store(query=query, top_k=5) print("\nResults:") print(format_search_results(results)) except Exception as error: print(f"Search error: {error}") def main() -> None: """Run the app.""" print("\nPersonal Knowledge Search Engine") print("=" * 50) print("1. Index notes") print("2. Search notes") print("=" * 50) choice = input("\nChoose an option: ").strip() if choice == "1": index_notes() elif choice == "2": search_loop() else: print("Unknown option.") if __name__ == "__main__": main() Test result: Python syntax check passed.

5.17 File: test_note_loader.py

Create test_note_loader.py:

from pathlib import Path import pytest from note_loader import ( is_supported_file, load_note_file, load_notes_from_folder, ) def test_is_supported_file(): assert is_supported_file(Path("note.md")) is True assert is_supported_file(Path("note.txt")) is True assert is_supported_file(Path("note.pdf")) is False def test_load_note_file(tmp_path: Path): note = tmp_path / "note.md" note.write_text("# Test Note\nHello world", encoding="utf-8") document = load_note_file(note) assert document.path == str(note) assert "Hello world" in document.text def test_load_note_file_missing(tmp_path: Path): missing = tmp_path / "missing.md" with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError): load_note_file(missing) def test_load_note_file_unsupported(tmp_path: Path): file = tmp_path / "note.pdf" file.write_text("fake pdf", encoding="utf-8") with pytest.raises(ValueError): load_note_file(file) def test_load_notes_from_folder(tmp_path: Path): (tmp_path / "a.md").write_text("A note", encoding="utf-8") (tmp_path / "b.txt").write_text("B note", encoding="utf-8") (tmp_path / "c.pdf").write_text("Unsupported", encoding="utf-8") documents = load_notes_from_folder(str(tmp_path)) assert len(documents) == 2 def test_load_notes_from_missing_folder(): with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError): load_notes_from_folder("missing_folder") Test result: Python syntax check passed.

Create test_text_utils.py:

import pytest from text_utils import clean_text, chunk_text, create_chunks_for_document def test_clean_text(): assert clean_text("Hello world\nagain") == "Hello world again" def test_chunk_text_returns_chunks(): text = "Python AI agents are useful. " * 100 chunks = chunk_text(text, chunk_size=100, overlap=20) assert len(chunks) > 1 assert all(len(chunk) <= 100 for chunk in chunks) def test_chunk_text_empty(): assert chunk_text(" ") == [] def test_chunk_text_invalid_size(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): chunk_text("hello", chunk_size=0) def test_chunk_text_invalid_overlap(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): chunk_text("hello", chunk_size=100, overlap=100) def test_create_chunks_for_document(): text = "Python AI agents are useful. Create test_vector_store_helpers.py:

5.21 How the Code Works

This project has five major stages.

Stage 1: Load Notes

The app loads Markdown and text files from the notes/ folder.

documents = load_notes_from_folder("notes")

Each document includes:

path text

Stage 2: Chunk Notes

Each note is split into chunks.

chunks = create_chunks_for_document( source=document.path, text=document.text, )

Each chunk includes:

id text source chunk_index

This metadata helps show where search results came from.

Stage 3: Create Embeddings

The embedding client converts chunk text into numeric vectors.

embeddings = embedder.embed_texts(texts)

Each text chunk becomes a vector.

Stage 4: Store in Chroma

The vector store saves:

chunk id chunk text embedding metadata

This makes the chunks searchable by meaning.

Stage 5: Search by Meaning

When the user enters a query, the app creates a query embedding and searches the vector database.

results = search_vector_store(query="How do agents use tools?")

The closest chunks are displayed.

5.23 Testing the Project

Run:

pytest

Expected type of result:

15 passed

The exact number and timing may vary if you add more tests.

These tests check:

  • Note loading
  • Supported file detection
  • Chunking
  • Chunk metadata
  • Search result formatting

The tests do not call the live embedding API.

That is intentional.

Embedding calls can cost money and require network access.

Test normal Python logic separately.

5.24 Live Embedding Test

After adding your API key to .env, run:

python search_app.py

Choose:

1. Index notes

Then run the app again and choose:

2. Search notes

Try:

How do agents remember things?

If your sample note includes memory-related text, the search should return the chunk about memory.

5.25 Debugging Semantic Search

Semantic search can fail too.

Common problems:

ProblemLikely CauseFix
No resultsNotes not indexedRun indexing first
Old resultsDatabase contains old chunksDelete chroma_db/ and reindex
Bad resultsPoor chunksAdjust chunk size
API errorMissing keyCheck .env
Duplicate resultsIndexed same notes multiple timesClear database before reindexing
Slow indexingLarge notesIndex fewer files first
Poor relevanceQuery too vagueAsk more specific question

A simple reset is:

rm -rf chroma_db

Then reindex.

On Windows PowerShell:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force chroma_db

5.26 Embeddings and Metadata

Embeddings help find meaning.

Metadata helps explain results.

A chunk without metadata is harder to trust.

Good metadata might include:

source file page number chunk index document title created date document type

This chapter stores:

source chunk_index

That is enough for a beginner project.

In stronger apps, add more metadata.

5.27 How This Improves Chapter 4

Chapter 4 answered questions about PDFs using keyword retrieval.

Chapter 5 adds semantic search.

The next improvement is combining them:

PDF ↓ Extract text ↓ Chunk text ↓ Embed chunks ↓ Store in vector database ↓ Search by meaning ↓ Answer using retrieved context

That is a stronger RAG system.

You can upgrade Chapter 4 by replacing the keyword retriever with the vector store from this chapter.

5.30 Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Confusing Embeddings with Chat Responses

Embeddings return numbers.

LLMs return text.

Use embeddings for search.

Use LLMs for answers.

Mistake 2: Forgetting to Store Metadata

Without metadata, users cannot tell where results came from.

Always store source information.

Mistake 3: Reindexing Without Clearing Duplicates

If you add the same chunks repeatedly, results may duplicate.

Clear or update the database carefully.

Mistake 4: Testing Only One Query

Try different wording.

Semantic search should handle related meaning, not just exact words.

Mistake 5: Ignoring Chunk Quality

Bad chunks lead to bad search.

Chunking still matters.

Mistake 6: Sending Secrets in Notes

Do not index API keys, passwords, private tokens, or confidential data unless you have proper security and permission.

Mistake 7: Treating Distance Scores as Universal

Vector database distance scores may vary by system and configuration.

Use them as relative signals, not absolute truth.

5.31 Best Practices

Chunk text before embedding.

Store source metadata.

Use meaningful collection names.

Keep local databases out of Git.

Clear and reindex when changing chunking strategy.

Test multiple query styles.

Avoid indexing secrets.

Use embeddings for retrieval and LLMs for generation.

Inspect search results before building answers.

Document limitations in README.

  • Semantic search finds results by meaning, not only keywords.
